messages.text: 'Not many sports teams have done it' - Wolff 'proud' of Mercedes turnaround

metadata.summary: Toto Wolff says he's "proud" of Mercedes' turnaround to win the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship and feels very few sports teams have bounced back so quickly.
metadata.content: Toto Wolff 'proud' of Mercedes turnaround after winning F1 2026 Constructors' Championship at Sao Paulo Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Toto Wolff 'proud' of Mercedes turnaround after winning F1 2026 Constructors' Championship at Sao Paulo Grand Prix Mercedes won their ninth F1 Constructors' Championship with three races to spare of the 2026 season; Mercedes won eight in a row between 2014 and 2021 before a fallow period and Toto Wolff is particularly proud of how the Silver Arrows bounced back Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 8 November 2026 22:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes party on the podium after sealing their ninth Constructors' Championship title Toto Wolff says he's "proud" of Mercedes' turnaround to win the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship and feels very few sports teams have bounced back so quickly. Mercedes won their ninth constructors' title on Sunday at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, five years after their last championship, which was their eighth in a row at the time. Regulation changes in 2022 ended Mercedes' dominance as they struggled to get on top of the so-called ground effect cars, but they have won the first season of the new 2026 cars, and also wrapped up the Drivers' Championship earlier this month with Kimi Antonelli. messages.text: Hamilton says he overrode Ferrari pit call due to 'lack of information'

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton says a lack of information led to him overriding Ferrari's call for him to come into the pits as rain fell during the closing stages of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says he overrode team's pit call due to 'lack of information' provided as rain fell during Sao Paulo GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says he overrode team's pit call due to 'lack of information' provided as rain fell during Sao Paulo GP Lewis Hamilton finished ninth in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix as Ferrari endured a disappointing weekend in Brazil; Hamilton lost out late in the race after ignoring a call to come into the pits to switch from slick to intermediate tyres as rain intensified Sunday 8 November 2026 22:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton nearly crashes out in the rain before entering the pits on slick tyres. Lewis Hamilton says a lack of information led to him overriding Ferrari's call for him to come into the pits as rain fell during the closing stages of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Hamilton was running in eighth at Interlagos when heavy rain began to fall with 10 laps to go. While the leaders had already passed the pit entry by the time the rain intensified, Mercedes brought in George Russell from fifth. Ferrari instructed Hamilton to come in, but he decided to do the opposite to the car just in front of him at the time, Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc, running just behind him, came into the pits. Sao Paulo GP race result F1 2026 Calendar | F1 2026 Standings | F1 Gossip Column Got the Sky Sports app? Sig

messages.text: Norris wins wet Sao Paulo GP as Mercedes seal constructors' title

metadata.summary: McLaren's Lando Norris recovered from a poor start to claim a dominant victory in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix that saw Mercedes seal the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Lando Norris wins wet race for McLaren as Mercedes seal 2026 F1 Constructors' Championship in Brazil | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP: Lando Norris wins wet race for McLaren as Mercedes seal 2026 F1 Constructors' Championship in Brazil Pole-sitter Lando Norris recovers from poor start to win Sao Paulo GP; Max Verstappen comes from 21st on grid to take second ahead of Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar; George Russell and Kimi Antonelli fourth and fifth, respectively, to seal Constructors' Championship for Mercedes Sunday 8 November 2026 21:40, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix. McLaren's Lando Norris recovered from a poor start to claim a dominant victory in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix that saw Mercedes seal the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship. Max Verstappen produced a signature stunning drive in the wet to come from 21st on the grid to finish second, with his team-mate Isack Hadjar completing a double-podium for Red Bull. Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli had looked on course for victory after taking the lead at the start but ultimately had to settle for fifth behind his team-mate George Russell, which was more than enough for Mercedes to establish an unassailable lead over Ferrari in the constructors' standings with three rounds to spare. messages.text: Villa boss Emery explains why he went down tunnel before full-time

metadata.summary: A prickly Unai Emery claimed he headed down the Old Trafford tunnel after Manchester United's late equaliser against his Aston Villa side because he thought the match was about to end.
metadata.content: Unai Emery: Aston Villa boss reveals why he went down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time in eight-goal thriller at Man Utd | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Unai Emery: Aston Villa boss reveals why he went down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time in eight-goal thriller at Man Utd Unai Emery headed down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time after Man Utd rescued a 4-4 draw against his Aston Villa team; Patrick Dorgu scored late equaliser in thrilling contest; Villa director of football operations Damian Vidagany questioned legitimacy of last goal Sunday 8 November 2026 20:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aston Villa boss Unai Emery explains his decision to walk down the tunnel at Old Trafford after Manchester United nabbed their 96th minute equaliser. A prickly Unai Emery claimed he headed down the Old Trafford tunnel after Manchester United's late equaliser against his Aston Villa side because he thought the match was about to end. Villa threw away two separate two-goal leads to draw 4-4 with United in a Super Sunday thriller - but the 97th-minute equaliser from Michael Carrick's side, scored by Patrick Dorgu, brought about a strange reaction from Emery. The Villa manager was seen walking down the tunnel before the full-time whistle, with the match continuing for another two minutes before it ended.
